title: Build-Your-Own Pho Bar
shortDescription: Vietnamese pho bar with broth, noodles, and herbs for ten
subtitle: Vietnamese pho bar with broth, noodles, and herbs for ten
description: A rich beef broth stays hot in a large pot while rice noodles, thin-sliced beef, herbs, bean sprouts, and sauces fill a build bar. Each bowl is assembled fresh so noodles stay separate from broth until serving.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Build-Your-Own Pho Bar in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Build aromatic broth
steps.instruction: Char ginger and onion under broiler 5 minutes. Simmer broth with star anise, cinnamon, ginger, and onion 90 minutes. Strain and keep at a bare simmer at 200°F for service.

steps.title: Prep proteins and noodles
steps.instruction: Slice partially frozen sirloin paper-thin across the grain. Cook rice noodles per package, rinse, toss with oil, and hold warm in a hotel pan.

steps.title: Set the pho bar
steps.instruction: Arrange noodles, raw beef slices, bean sprouts, basil, cilantro, lime wedges, and green onions in separate pans. Place hoisin, sriracha, and fish sauce at the end.

steps.title: Assemble bowls to order
steps.instruction: Portion noodles into bowls, top with raw beef slices, and ladle boiling broth over top—the hot broth cooks beef to medium-rare in the bowl. Verify broth reads 190°F when ladled.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Build-Your-Own Pho Bar onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Finish with herbs and serve
steps.instruction: Crew adds sprouts, herbs, lime, and hoisin or sriracha as each person prefers. Serve immediately while broth is steaming—pho does not hold well once noodles and beef are in the bowl.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Build-Your-Own Pho Bar — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Fish sauce added at the table lets individuals control funk level without scaring newcomers.
Mushrooms or tofu slices offer a vegetarian path through the same bar setup.
Wide bowls dissipate heat slower—crew can eat sooner without tongue burns.
tonightSpread: Pho bar with simmering broth, noodles, beef, and full herb plate.
Spring rolls or edamame from the store for a light starter while broth finishes.
leftovers: Broth freezes excellently—reheat and run pho bar again with fresh noodles.
Slice leftover beef into stir-fry with the bean sprouts and green onions.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Pho feels like a treat but scales well for a hall. The build-your-own format handles different spice tolerances and the hot broth is genuinely restorative after cold-weather calls.
mealPrepNotes: Broth can simmer hours ahead or use a doctored store base on tight timelines. Freeze beef 30 minutes for easy thin slicing. Cook noodles just before service and toss with oil.
